theorem_title: A Sidon subset of $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ of size at least $\sqrt{N}/4$
natural_language_statement:
For every $N$ there is a Sidon set inside $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ with at least $\sqrt{N}/4$ elements.

Two regimes. For $N \le 144$ the fixed set $\{0, 1, 3\}$ already has three elements and $\sqrt{144}/4 = 3$, and for $N < 4$ the singleton $\{0\}$ does. For $N > 144$ take $m = \lfloor\sqrt{N/2}\rfloor/2$ and apply Bertrand's postulate to get a prime $p$ with $m < p \le 2m$. Then $2p^2 \le N$, so the previous statement puts the Erdos-Turan set inside the interval, and $p > m$ beats $\sqrt{N}/4$.

Every later milestone pigeonholes a set against this one. It is also the one place in the development where a Sidon set is constructed; everywhere else a Sidon set is found inside something given.
source: Paul Erdos and Pal Turan, "On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory, and on some related problems", J. London Math. Soc. 16 (1941) 212-215; the constant $1/4$ is a convenient weakening
